focus: Unread ground: edge cases in the reducer and the append gateway — duplicate iteration number, status error row, delta finding rows without type finding, empty or malformed delta line, two concurrent writers

graphEvents.label: Do reducer and gateway edge cases fail closed?

label: Delta-file corruption is fail-open while state-log corruption is fail-closed: parseJsonlDetailed collects per-line corruptionWarnings but loadDeltaPayloads only console.warns them, and the reducer exit-2 gate is bound to the state-log warnings alone, so a malformed delta line — the artifact the leaf contract makes primary — costs one stderr line and exit 0. No test covers delta corruption; the state-log case is covered by deep-research-reduce-state.vitest.ts:381.
verify: grep -n corruptionWarnings .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs; then a tmp delta dir with one broken line and reduce --emit-resource-map

label: Duplicate iteration rows are never deduped and both the count and the latest-iteration selection key on row position, not iteration number: records are filtered by type only, iterationsCompleted counts rows, and latestIteration is .at(-1) rather than max(iteration). A redispatch that appends a second row for iteration N inflates the completed count, renders two dashboard rows numbered N, and lets the last-appended row drive dashboard status. append-mode-event-cli.vitest.ts:232 covers sequential appends of distinct records only.
verify: append the same type:iteration record twice with a differing newInfoRatio, then reduce and read progress.iterationsCompleted

label: iter-23.jsonl and iter-023.jsonl both satisfy the delta filename regex, so one iteration number can be supplied twice and collectDeltaIterationRecords silently keeps the first — the zero-padded spelling wins the numeric-aware sort — discarding the other file's answeredQuestions with no warning. No test covers two spellings in one directory; the same-named-file test at deep-research-reduce-state.vitest.ts:280 aggregates across lineage directories instead.
verify: create deltas/iter-023.jsonl and deltas/iter-23.jsonl with different answeredQuestions and diff the strategy box ticks

label: A status:error iteration row is half-counted: correctly excluded from question coverage, but still counted in iterationsCompleted and still eligible as the last-appended latest iteration that drives dashboard status, because deriveDashboardStatus special-cases only stuck. The same filter defaults a missing status to complete via String(record.status || complete), so a malformed row silently becomes coverage-eligible. append-mode-event-cli.vitest.ts:752 proves only that the projection keeps an error row across a later append.
verify: seed one status:error row carrying answeredQuestions for Q1, run reduce --lenient, confirm Q1 unticked while iterationsCompleted is 1

label: The delta finding discriminator is unread by the reducer: the literal finding appears zero times in the 3351-line file, and the only record.type discriminators are event and iteration. Registry findings come from the iteration markdown Findings section and from a record's own findings array, so the contract rule that every finding row must carry type:finding is unenforced by any consumer read this iteration. The real risk is the asymmetry: a leaf writing findings only to the delta file and abbreviating the narrative section loses them from the registry, while one omitting the type field loses nothing.

Malformed delta lines are replaced by fabricated null rows — records.concat(new Array(n).fill(null)) — so payload length survives and non-records flow into deltaSourceCount and every delta consumer. collectDeltaIterationRecords guards for it, but the resource-map sources extractor was not read, so a row.sources dereference there throwing on a null row is inferred, not confirmed; a delta file with one good and one broken line plus --emit-resource-map is the check that settles it. No test covers the padding.
verify: feed a one-good one-broken delta file to reduce-state --emit-resource-map and read the exit status

label: Two concurrent appends cannot corrupt the ledger — exclusive store lock on both getVerifiedHead and append, fence_token in the frame and header allowlists, and a prior_head_sequence !== frame.sequence - 1 validation reject the stale writer — but the CLI seeds prevEventHash and streamSequence from a head read taken outside that lock, never retries, and lets the rejection escape as phase runtime exit 1, while the packing contract documents exit 2 as the refusal signal. An unattended run therefore reports a generic runtime error instead of a fencing refusal. append-mode-event-cli.vitest.ts asserts exit 2 for authority, binding and mode refusals only, and has no concurrent-writer case.
verify: run two append-mode-event.cjs processes against one run directory in the background and print both exit statuses

direction: Two writers appending at once corrupt the deep-research ledger bytes.
reason: Refuted: AppendOnlyLedger takes an exclusive store lock for both the head read and the append, frames carry a fence_token, and prior_head_sequence is validated. The defect is the CLI exit code and its missing retry, not the frame chain.

direction: The numeric-aware delta sort makes iter-23 / iter-023 collisions deterministic and therefore safe.
reason: Refuted: localeCompare numeric-aware ordering does order the padded name first, but byIteration.has() then drops the other file silently. Deterministic is not the same as warned or correct.
